title: Prefix cache integrity incident — action items and tracking
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-28 we observed a distributed degradation across prefix-cache-backed routes leading to elevated tail latency and reduced throughput for hosted inference customers. Root cause analysis shows two interacting bugs: (1) a prefix-key normalization omission allowed semantically-equivalent keys (different encodings/whitespace) to collide and cause stale entries to be treated as authoritative (cache poisoning), and (2) a weighted-eviction accounting bug caused incorrect resident set size calculations, which in some workloads prevented eviction and led to gradual memory growth and OOMs on a subset of nodes. The combination meant some nodes served poisoned prefixes while others experienced memory pressure and GC pauses. Impact: customer-facing latency spikes, increased 5xx rate for ~45 minutes, and two Dedicated pools required rolling restarts to recover. This ticket scopes the follow-up action plan, ownership, rollout plan, and telemetry to prevent recurrence.
action_items: AI-1: Add deterministic prefix normalization at ingestion boundary (trim, unicode-normalize, canonicalize separators). Owner: Miguel Santos. Due: 2026-03-10. Status: Done in branch fix/prefix-normalize; merged 2026-03-05.

AI-2: Add regression tests covering encoded/whitespace variants + fuzz harness for prefix inputs. Owner: Priya Narang. Due: 2026-03-12. Status: In Review (PR: https://github.com/redwood/serving/pull/2419).

AI-3: Fix weighted-eviction accounting: correct byte-weight calc and add unit + integration tests for eviction under skewed key-size distributions. Owner: Liang Wu. Due: 2026-03-15. Status: In Progress.

AI-4: Implement memory-leak detection instrumentation in hotpath (allocation counters, slab usage metrics) and export to Prometheus. Owner: SRE Team (oncall: Elena Kim). Due: 2026-03-18. Status: In Progress.

AI-5: Add end-to-end canary rollout plan for patch: canary 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback if OOMs or 5xx > baseline. Owner: Release Engineering (Grant Powell). Due: 2026-03-20. Status: Planned.

AI-6: Add alerting rule for sudden divergence in prefix-hit-distribution across nodes and for eviction-rate anomalies. Owner: Observability (Nikita Rao). Due: 2026-03-14. Status: Done (alert ID: obs-evict-112).

AI-7: Run a capacity test with synthetic traffic that reproduces mixed-encoding workload and monitor cache metrics for 72h. Owner: Performance Engineering (Ana Torres). Due: 2026-03-22. Status: Scheduled.

AI-8: Document operational runbook for prefix-cache poisoning scenarios (symptoms, quick mitigations, safe restart sequence). Owner: Miguel Santos. Due: 2026-03-13. Status: Done (confluence link below).
AI-9: Postmortem writeup and customer communications draft for affected customers. Owner: Customer Success (Riley Chen). Due: 2026-03-07. Status: Done.

AI-10: Audit code paths that perform custom serialization/deserialization of cache entries and remove any non-idempotent transforms. Owner: Research/Applied ML (Tomás Vega). Due: 2026-03-21. Status: In Progress.

AI-11: Backfill historical telemetry to estimate frequency of malformed prefixes in production over the last 90 days. Owner: Observability (Nikita Rao). Due: 2026-03-14. Status: Done; attached dashboard link.
mitigation_steps_taken: Short-term: Rolled targeted restarts of affected Dedicated pools to clear poisoned entries (2026-02-28 16:20-16:50 UTC).

Hotfix: Deployed prefix-normalization hotfix to hosted nodes behind canary (1% traffic) within 12 hours; observed reduction in divergent hit patterns. PR: https://github.com/redwood/serving/pull/2410.
Traffic-level: Temporarily throttled a small set of client keys exhibiting high mutation patterns while investigating.
